# hosting.redirects — _redirects has a malformed line or redirects to a path the built site does not serve

- **Check ID:** `hosting.redirects`
- **Default severity:** `error`; users can override it in `seaworthy.config.json`.
- **Needs:** `files`
- **Standards:** Netlify redirects, Cloudflare Pages redirects
- **Source module:** `packages/verify/src/checks/hosting.ts`
- **Prose page:** [`docs/checks/hosting.redirects.md`](../hosting.redirects.md) — embedded below verbatim; write it there, never here.

The `_redirects` file of Netlify or Cloudflare Pages has a malformed line, or a redirect points at a path the built site does not serve.

## Why it matters

Both hosts read `_redirects` top to bottom and silently ignore lines they cannot parse, so a malformed rule quietly stops redirecting. A rule that points at a file the build does not have is worse: everyone who uses the moved link lands on a 404, and search engines lose the link the redirect was meant to keep.

## What it checks

- A rule line holds a source path, a destination, an optional status code (with `!` to force it), and conditions like `Country=de`, separated by spaces. Source and rule shape follow both hosts' documented syntax; a 404 or 410 rule may omit the destination.
- The source has at most one splat, ending the path, and placeholder segments like `:year` start right after the `/`.
- A destination that is a plain path matches a page or file in the build. Destinations with question marks or placeholders, and full `https://` addresses, are left alone.
- A source that repeats an earlier rule with the same conditions becomes dead code, because the first matching rule wins. The later rule is reported as a warning.
- A rule that redirects a path to itself with a redirect status (301, 302, 303, 307, 308) loops forever in the browser.

## How to fix

Point the destination at a page the build emits, or build the page it should land on. Fix malformed lines the way the hosts document:

```text
# before: a bare word is silently ignored
/old-page new-page

# after
/old-page /new-page/ 301
```

Change the source that produces the built `_redirects` file, not just the build output.

## Options

None.

## Standards

- [Netlify: redirects and rewrites](https://docs.netlify.com/manage/routing/redirects/overview/)
- [Cloudflare Pages: redirects](https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/configuration/redirects/)
